relationships.subject: Dorsal root ganglion stimulation
relationships.evidence_quote: DRG-S is postulated to offer analgesic benefits by potentially intensifying this filtering characteristic within the DRG neurons implicated in pain pathophysiology, thereby further modulating pain perception.

relationships.subject: Dorsal root ganglion stimulation
relationships.evidence_quote: It is proposed that the efficacy of DRG-S in CRPS is due to the inhibition of noxious and autonomic afferent signals at the T-junction and linked to the activation of the endogenous opioid systems in the dorsal horn.

key_findings: DRG-S analgesia is proposed to arise from T-junction filtering, dorsal horn gating and altered DRG neuron excitability; mechanism differs from GABA-dependent SCS.
DRG-S is FDA-approved for CRPS lower-extremity pain; evidence beyond CRPS is limited.
